## you need github version of ggtree and treeio

edge = x@phylo$edge
edge = as.data.frame(edge)
edge = edge[edge[,2] <= Ntip(x), ]

df = x@data
merge(df, edge, by.x="node", by.y="V1", all.x=F, all.y=T) -> df2
df3= df2[, c(3, 2)]
colnames(df3) = colnames(df)
x@data = rbind(df3, df)

ggtree(x, aes(size=I(support/100)))

messages.body_plain:
I would like to plot 2 phylogenies in a multiplot with pie charts and I want to have the reverse of the second phylogeny. However if I inverse the x-axis of the phylogeny the pie charts are not plotted in the inverse.

For example, this works fine:

> set.seed(1)
> tr <- rtree(4)
> p <- ggtree(tr)
> pie <- nodepie(p$data, cols = 4:5)
> inset(p, pie)

But when I invert the tree the pie-charts are not plotted on the corresponding nodes:

> p <- p+ scale_x_reverse()
> inset(p, pie)

How can I invert the x-axis of the pie charts?

messages.subject: only colour tip branches
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have been using groupOTU to color the branches on a tree base on IUCN red list status, but it does not make sense to colour the internal branches of the tree, which happens with groupOTU.

is there a method to just color the branches that are associated with tips?

When using APE for this I would do the following

# make a vector of color for all edges in the tree
edge.col <- rep("black", dim(tree$edge)[1])
# get the edge index for each branch under a tip - taken from BioGeoBears Package
tip.branches <- get_indices_of_branches_under_tips(tree)
# substitute tip branch colors in edge.col with a vector of color for tips that are order by tree$tip.label
edge.col[tip.branches] <- tip.colours

# plot with edge.color = edge.col
plot(tree, type = "fan", show.tip.label = F, edge.color = edge.col)

Might there be away to alter groupOTU to specify whether only tip branch or internal branches are to be colored?

Thanks!

ggtree is an awesome packages and keeps getting better!

Pete

messages.subject: MSA plot alt coloring options
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was wondering if there is a way to change the coloring in the msa plots so that each sequence is colored by gene rather than by base pair. I work with HIV, which can be rather different within and between participants. I think the easiest way would be if I could specify what proportion of the alignment I would like to contribute to a gene. For example, color the first 1% of the alignment blue to correspond to the LTR and the next 17% purple for the GAG gene. I realise that the best way would be to define gene breakpoints, but that is rather difficult with HIV's diversity. When we sequence full genomes, we see a lot of large deletions, and we would like to be able to communicate which genes those break points are in with colors. I have attached an example of what we would ideally like to be able to generate below. Alternatively, it would be good to be able to color the whole sequence by cell type similar to the colors I have filled the symbols with. Thank you for all of your great work on this package. Will hopefully be able to cite it in a new paper soon!

Thanks,
Kirston

If one internal node connects to two clades, each being a different OTU, the function produces the expected results, i.e., a black edge after the clades coalesce to the same common ancestor: Like green and red OTUs in this tree.

library(ggtree)

tree <- rtree(14)

            c2=c("t1","t11","t2"))

tree <- groupOTU(tree, cls)
ggtree(tree, aes(color=group)) + geom_text(aes(label=label)) +

  scale_color_manual(values=c("black", "red","green")) + theme(legend.position="right")

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-D43hrC3UHN0/WIYgC9ZIMTI/AAAAAAAAAIM/ZUMN_r_kbM8B2vsugp7PGZzG17MG3TV9wCLcB/s1600/Correct.png>

Now, if one tip belonging to, lets say, OTU "blue" connects to a node and it happens that that node is connected to two or more tips of a different OTU "green", the results is that the edges starting from that node towards the root of the tree will have the same color of the tip that is connected to the node, i.e, blue, like here with t2 and t3:

  scale_color_manual(values=c("black", "red","green")) + theme(legend.position="right")
